title: Design Details
summary: Students identify visible garment details, connect them to function and visual effect, read and listen to short detail captions, and produce one scaffolded detail-caption card.
essential_question: How can I describe garment design details clearly in simple English?
professional_context: Week 11 connects English to early critique, sketch annotation, sewing and patternmaking observation, and short portfolio-caption language. Students move from describing a full sketch to naming and explaining specific design details such as closures, pockets, trims, and decorative finishes.
language_focus: detail naming for closures, pockets, decorative features, and construction details
location phrases such as on the front, near the neckline, and at the side
There is and There are for visible design details
frames such as It is placed ..., It is functional because ..., It is decorative because ..., It adds ..., and It makes ...
grammar_focus: on the front / near the neckline / at the side
teacher_preparation: Preview the opener board, the vocabulary board, the scavenger garment, and the reusable detail gallery before class.
Keep the key labels exactly stable as image A to image D and point A to point H where the activities depend on those labels.
Keep the main writing task as six required short lines plus one optional challenge line. Do not convert it into a paragraph or add a word-count target.
Check that the Week 11 listening gallery, the audio script, the question labels, and the correct answers all match exactly before using the listening task.
Prepare quick correction support for There is / There are, article use, functional versus decorative, and short location phrases.
Decide whether students will use projected garment-detail images, printed cards, or teacher-provided references during the speaking session.
student_deliverables: Completion of the Week 11 opener selections.
Completion of the main design-detail vocabulary matching set.
Completion of one visual scavenger matching task plus short role checks for functional, decorative, or both.
Reading-comprehension responses matching short detail captions to image A, image B, image C, or image D and answering detail-meaning questions.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying details from one short numbered listening clip.
Completion of five phrase-practice fill blanks for location, effect, and function language.
A scaffolded Design Detail Caption Set card with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge line.
Two corrected Week 11 detail-caption sentences saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral explanation of one design detail.
